commands.review_summary:
The PR changes Android Compose and shared SwiftUI chat views to preserve reader position, add Jump to latest behavior, update native i18n inventory, and add focused native tests.

PR surface: Other +1129. Total +1129 across 14 files.

Reproducibility: yes. for the blocking review findings: source inspection shows Android onViewportChanged and iOS onScrollPhaseChange leave the jump affordance hidden when a reader manually scrolls away from the live edge with no new content arriving. The broader feature is proven by simulator/emulator output rather than a current-main failing test.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow automation repair can address the two remaining native scroll-state findings without deciding the broader product direction.

target.title: improve: make native chat scrolling reader-managed
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native chat views currently move the transcript as messages, tool rows, and streaming text arrive. That can pull readers away from content they are reviewing in long or actively streaming conversations.

Fixes #98255.

## Why This Change Was Made

This gives iOS and Android an explicit reader-managed scrolling model:

- restore an opened conversation near the latest user turn instead of the absolute bottom
- preserve that user-turn anchor while assistant and tool content streams below it
- stop following when the reader scrolls away
- show **Jump to latest** when newer content is offscreen
- resume live-edge following only after the reader taps the control or sends a new message
- keep restored Android reader state scoped to the owning session

The repair removes the contributor's preview/debug proof harnesses. Production state transitions and the normal app UI test are the only paths retained.

## User Impact

- Reopening a session keeps the newest prompt visible for context.
- Sending a message intentionally brings the new turn into view.
- Manual reading position survives streaming and tool updates.
- **Jump to latest** exposes and then clears the paused-reader state predictably.

## Evidence

### iOS simulator end-to-end

The standard `OpenClawUITests` live-gateway scenario was extended to exercise the shipping app against an isolated local gateway. It sends an exact marker through `github-copilot/gpt-5.4`, verifies the exact reply, scrolls to the prompt anchor, asserts **Jump to latest**, then taps it and verifies the control disappears while the exact marker remains visible.

```text
PASS xcodebuild test -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClawUITests \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=E617A5DF-735E-442C-98EC-31C140517359' \
  -only-testing:OpenClawUITests/OpenClawSnapshotUITests/testLiveGatewayChatRoundTripAndControlOverview
```

Result bundle: `/tmp/pr98258-ios-final-head-green12.xcresult` (local maintainer artifact). Fresh baseline, prompt-anchor, and post-jump screenshots were inspected at 1206x2622. The configured Crabbox artifact broker is unavailable on this machine, so the screenshots were not uploaded to an external host.

### Android behavior and emulator proof

Focused controller and timeline tests cover restore, manual-scroll preservation, regenerated message IDs, newer-user transitions, tool/stream updates, jump-to-latest, and rejection of saved state from a different session. The repaired screen was also exercised in the Android emulator; fresh baseline, prompt-anchor, and post-jump screenshots were inspected at 1080x2400.

```text
PASS ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Library/Android/sdk" ./gradlew \
  :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.chat.ChatReaderScrollControllerTest \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.chat.ChatTimelineTest \
  :app:ktlintCheck
```

### Review

- Current `main` still lacks the behavior; the repaired head is rebased onto current `origin/main`.
- Whole-branch autoreview completed with no actionable findings after two fixes were added from earlier review passes.
- Native PR wrapper verified that the remote contributor branch tree exactly matches the repaired local tree.
